draft.title: Cell theory
card: Cell theory has three parts. All living things are made of one or more cells.
The cell is the basic unit of life. It is the smallest unit that can carry out the functions of life, such as growing, using energy and responding to its surroundings.
New cells come only from existing cells. Cells form by the division of a cell that was already there, not from non-living matter.
Some organisms are a single cell, such as an amoeba. Others, such as a eucalypt tree, are made of millions of cells.
draft.remember: Life is made of cells, cells are the basic unit, and cells come from cells.

a.q: A student says a single yeast cell is a whole living organism. Which part of cell theory supports this?
opts: The cell is the basic unit of life and can live on its own
New cells come only from existing cells
All cells must be part of a many-celled organism
Living things must contain at least two types of cell
a.why: A yeast cell carries out the functions of life by itself, so it is a complete organism. This fits the idea that the cell is the basic unit of life. The idea that new cells come from existing cells is about where cells arise, not about whether one cell can be an organism.
a.clue: Think about what a single cell can do on its own.

b.q: Mia sterilises a nutrient broth in a sealed flask and finds no cells in it. Weeks later it is still sealed and still has no cells. Which part of cell theory does this fit?
opts: New cells come only from existing cells
All living things are made of cells
The cell is the basic unit of life
Cells are the smallest living things on Earth
b.why: No cells appeared in the sealed broth because there were no existing cells to divide. This fits the idea that new cells come only from existing cells. The broth shows nothing about what living things are made of, which is why the first part is a weaker fit.
b.clue: Where could new cells in the flask have come from?

a.best: The cell is the basic unit of life and can live on its own

b.best: New cells come only from existing cells

problems.detail: The right option stands out. It is clearly the longest and the only one with an added detail ('and can live on its own'). Two distractors use 'must' and are plainly false, so a student can pick the answer without knowing the idea.

A eucalypt tree is made of far more than 'millions' of cells. A large tree has billions or more, so 'millions' understates the scale and could mislead. 'Many millions or billions' or simply 'very many cells' would be accurate.

proposal.title: Cell theory
card: Cell theory has three parts. The first is that all living things are made of one or more cells.

The second is that the cell is the basic unit of life. It is the smallest thing that can carry out the functions of life, such as growing, using energy and responding to its surroundings. Molecules inside a cell are smaller, but they cannot live on their own.
The third is that new cells come only from existing cells. Cells form when a cell that was already there divides, not from non-living matter.
Some organisms are a single cell, such as an amoeba. Others, such as a eucalypt tree, are made of billions of cells.
proposal.remember: Life is made of cells, cells are the basic unit, and cells come from cells.

a.q: What does it mean to say the cell is the basic unit of life?
opts: It is the smallest thing that can carry out life's functions
It is the smallest particle that makes up a living thing
It is a structure found only in organisms with many cells
It is the largest structure found inside a living thing
a.why: A cell is the smallest thing that can grow, use energy and respond by itself. It is not the smallest particle in a living thing: molecules inside a cell are smaller, but they cannot live on their own.
a.clue: Think about what can stay alive by itself.

b.q: Mia sterilises a nutrient broth in a sealed flask and finds no cells in it. Weeks later it is still sealed and still has no cells. Which idea does this fit?
opts: New cells come only from existing cells
All living things are made of cells
The cell is the basic unit of life
Living things can form from non-living matter
b.why: No cells appeared because there were no existing cells in the flask to divide. This fits the idea that new cells come only from existing cells. The result says nothing about what living things are made of, and it goes against the idea that life forms from non-living matter.
b.clue: Where could new cells in the flask have come from?

a.best: It is the smallest thing that can carry out life's functions

b.best: New cells come only from existing cells
